article.title: Why Percentages Need a Denominator
article.why: Build practical English through analytical and business reasoning.
article.author: OpenAI learning brief

paragraphs.en: Percentages are useful because they make different numbers easy to compare. But a percentage without its denominator can create the wrong impression. If one shop says complaints increased by 100 percent, that sounds serious. Yet the change may be from one complaint to two. Another shop may report only a 10 percent increase, but that could mean a rise from one hundred to one hundred and ten complaints. The percentage alone does not tell us the scale.
paragraphs.zh: 百分比方便比較不同數字，但如果沒有分母，很容易造成錯誤印象。某店說客訴增加100%，聽起來很嚴重，實際可能只是從1件變2件。另一店只增加10%，卻可能是100件變110件。只看百分比無法知道真正規模。
paragraphs.ja: 割合は比較に便利だが、分母がないと誤った印象を与える。苦情が100％増えた店でも1件から2件になっただけかもしれない。一方、10％増でも100件から110件なら実数は大きい。割合だけでは規模が分からない。

paragraphs.en: The same rule matters for conversion rates. A campaign with two purchases from ten customers has a 20 percent conversion rate. A campaign with one hundred and fifty purchases from one thousand customers has a lower rate of 15 percent, but it produces far more purchases. Which result is better depends on the goal, cost, and sample size. A high percentage from a tiny group can also move sharply when only one person changes behavior.
paragraphs.zh: 轉換率也是如此。10名顧客中2人購買是20%，1000人中150人購買只有15%，但後者實際購買數多得多。哪個結果更好，要看目標、成本與樣本數。小群體的高比例也可能因一個人改變行為就大幅波動。
paragraphs.ja: 成約率も同じである。10人中2人なら20％、1000人中150人なら15％だが、購入件数は後者が圧倒的に多い。どちらが良いかは目的、費用、標本数で変わる。小集団の高い割合は一人の変化だけで大きく動く。

paragraphs.en: Growth rates need context too. Revenue growing by 50 percent from a very small base may add less money than revenue growing by 5 percent in a large business. Discounts work similarly: 20 percent off tells you the relative reduction, but you still need the original price to know how much money you save. A percentage describes a relationship between numbers; it is not a complete description of the situation.
paragraphs.zh: 成長率也需要脈絡。很小的基期成長50%，增加的金額可能仍少於大型事業成長5%。折扣也是一樣：打八折只告訴你相對降幅，還需要原價才能知道實際省多少。百分比描述的是數字間的關係，而不是完整情況。
paragraphs.ja: 成長率にも文脈が必要だ。小さな基準から50％伸びても、大規模事業の5％成長より増加額が小さいことがある。20％引きも元値が分からなければ節約額は分からない。割合は数字同士の関係であり、状況全体の説明ではない。

paragraphs.en: A simple habit can prevent many mistakes: whenever you see a percentage, ask “out of how many?” Then look at both the rate and the count. If the number changed over time, check the starting value as well. This does not make percentages less useful. It makes them more useful because you can understand what the percentage actually represents and whether the change is large enough to matter.
paragraphs.zh: 簡單習慣可以避免很多錯誤：看到百分比就問「總共多少？」同時看比例與件數；若是時間上的變化，也確認起始值。這不會讓百分比變得沒用，反而能理解它真正代表什麼，以及變化是否大到值得關注。
paragraphs.ja: 簡単な習慣で誤解を防げる。割合を見たら「何件中か」と問い、率と件数を一緒に見る。時系列変化なら出発点も確認する。割合の価値が下がるのではなく、何を表し、その変化が重要な規模かを理解しやすくなる。
